newsitem.title: USA: Dole aide meets Perot, asks him to leave race - TV.
newsitem.headline: Dole aide meets Perot, asks him to leave race - TV.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole's campaign chairman travelled to Dallas to meet with Texas billionaire Ross Perot and ask him to drop out of the race, ABC News reported on Wednesday.

The report said the Dole campaign was asking the Reform Party candidate to end his presidential bid, which has attracted little enthusiasm according to polls, and endorse Dole in his effort to oust President Bill Clinton.

Reform Party officials said they were not aware of any meeting between Perot and Dole envoys, and flatly rejected suggestions that Perot might withdraw from the race despite his poor standing in the polls.
"There is absolutely no truth to that. He is in the race to the bitter end. No question," Perot's spokeswoman, Sharon Holmanm, said. "Furthermore, we expect to win."
Dole campaign officials refused to comment on the report.

Perot has attacked both Dole and Clinton equally throughout his campaign, claiming both men were dodging the real issues facing the country and their parties were corrupted by special interest groups.
Senior Reform Party officials also singled out Dole for criticism after the Republican candidate argued that Perot should not be allowed to participate in the televised presidential debates.
